newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $0.50 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were mostly steady early, instances $0.50 per cwt lower amid light packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant ranged mostly from $58.00 to $59.00. An extreme top of $59.50 was possible, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower, with a top of $57.00 in the country and $57.50 at plants.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant were mostly steady, with a top of $55.00 in the country and $58.00 at plants.

Several packer buyers said they had bought most of Friday's needed inventory Thursday and were almost finished buying for Monday. Saturday's slaughter was expected to be light, which further dampened packer buying interest.
Saturday's slaughter was estimated at 45,000 to 50,000 head by livestock market analysts, compared with the USDA statistics indicating a 40,000-head kill a week ago and 91,000 a year ago.
Packer interest also was diluted by large pork production at midweek, which trimmed wholesale pork prices which in turn, ate into operating margins, market sources said.
